channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: SonicWall SonicOS MFA Bypass Vulnerability Exploited
item.description: CISA has added the SonicWall 'SonicOS' MFA bypass flaw, CVE‑2026‑19868, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of real‑world exploitation. The vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 7.1/7.5, allows attackers to bypass multi‑factor authentication and gain unauthorized access to SonicWall devices. SonicWall has released a patch; administrators should update firmware promptly to mitigate the risk.

item.title: MSP Customers Question Attack Detection Capabilities
item.description: A Barracuda Networks survey shows companies outsourcing cybersecurity to MSPs doubt their attack detection. The report notes 66% of organizations already outsource security services, 29% are evaluating MSPs, yet recovery remains weak and AI risk management is a priority. Findings urge MSPs to improve detection, clarify risk implications, and strengthen recovery to meet client expectations.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Ruby 4.0 Security Update for RHEL 9
item.description: Red Hat released a Ruby 4.0 module update for RHEL 9, fixing multiple security bugs that could allow local privilege escalation. The update addresses vulnerabilities with a moderate CVSS base score, though no CVE IDs are listed in the advisory. Security teams should apply the ruby:4.0 update promptly to mitigate the identified weaknesses and maintain system integrity.

item.title: Hackers Log In Within 8 Minutes Using Stolen Credentials
item.description: Attackers leveraged stolen credentials to log into compromised systems an average of eight minutes after initial infection across 27 infostealer incidents. The report also noted attackers used AI tools to execute commands and signed remote monitoring software to sustain persistence. Security teams should enforce multi‑factor authentication, monitor credential usage, and deploy rapid credential‑rotation policies to mitigate this threat.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Ruby 3.3 Security Update for RHEL 9

The advisory notes a moderate CVSS base score for each vulnerability, but no specific CVE identifiers are provided. Apply the ruby:3.3 update promptly to close the identified weaknesses and maintain system security.

item.title: Red Hat Releases curl Security Update
item.description: Red Hat has issued a 'curl' security update for Enterprise Linux 10, addressing critical vulnerabilities identified in the software. The update carries an Important security impact rating, and each vulnerability is linked to a CVE entry with a CVSS base score. Administrators should apply the RHSA‑2026:96092 update immediately to protect against the disclosed flaws.

item.title: Red Hat Issues squid:4 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat has released a security update for the 'squid:4' module on Enterprise Linux 8, addressing identified vulnerabilities that could allow remote code execution. The update is rated Important, and each vulnerability is referenced by a CVE with an associated CVSS score. Administrators should apply the RHSA‑2026:96078 update promptly to mitigate the risks.

item.title: RHSA-2026:96080: Important: webkit2gtk3 security update
item.description: An update for webkit2gtk3 is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Red Hat Releases gdb Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a gdb security update for RHEL 9.6 Extended Update Support, fixing multiple bugs. Red Hat advises applying the update immediately; no workarounds are required for security.

item.title: Claude AI Deletes Law Professor’s Syllabus
item.description: Anthropic’s Claude AI mistakenly removed a Chicago law professor’s entire syllabus and a year of lecture notes during a routine editing task. The loss was recovered from Dropbox, preventing permanent data loss, but the incident highlights accidental deletion risks in AI-assisted workflows. Users should back up critical documents and monitor AI outputs to mitigate similar accidental deletions.

The update mitigates several Qt base bugs with CVSS scores provided in CVE references, which could allow local privilege escalation or denial of service. Red Hat recommends applying the qt5-qtbase update immediately; no additional workarounds are needed.

item.title: NVIDIA Investigates Suspected Chinese Spy Operation
item.description: NVIDIA opened an independent investigation into reports that a foreign intelligence operation targeted CEO Jensen Huang. The review will examine the alleged activity and any potential security impact, though the board states no evidence of company secrets or national security compromise. Security teams should monitor for related phishing or credential theft attempts and ensure multi-factor authentication for executive accounts.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Ruby Update for RHEL 9.8
item.description: A moderate security update addresses multiple Ruby vulnerabilities affecting Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support. The update mitigates unspecified code execution risks identified in Ruby's core libraries, with CVSS scores available via referenced CVE links. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately; no workarounds are required to ensure system integrity.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical OpenShift 4.19.55 Update
item.description: Red Hat released OpenShift Container Platform 4.19.55, addressing multiple critical bugs and security flaws affecting cluster management components. The update mitigates privilege escalation and code execution risks identified in the platform's API server and scheduler, with CVSS scores linked via CVE references. Red Hat advises applying the update immediately; no workarounds are available, and users should verify cluster integrity post‑deployment.

item.title: OpenShift 4.20.46 Releases Critical Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released OpenShift 4.20.46, adding bug fixes and security updates for the 4.20 series. The update carries a Critical rating, with CVSS scores linked to each CVE, indicating high exploitation risk. Red Hat has made 4.20.46 available; teams should apply the update or upgrade images immediately to mitigate risks.

item.title: React Server Components RCE Flaw Exposes Remote Code Execution
item.description: A critical flaw in React Server Components allows unauthenticated remote code execution across react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel, and react-server-dom-turbopack. The vulnerability, tracked as GHSA-xqc2-xf4c-x3h3, carries a CVSS v4 score of 9.5, indicating a severe exploitation risk. React recommends immediate updates to affected applications; no workaround is available, and security teams should apply patches promptly.

item.title: ISC Stormcast Podcast Released November 9, 2026
item.description: The SANS Internet Storm Center released the ISC Stormcast podcast for Monday, November 9, 2026. The episode covers current threat landscape trends, emerging attack vectors, and defensive best practices, featuring expert commentary. Listeners can access the recording via the ISC website, with Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 license permitting sharing and adaptation.

item.title: OpenShift 4.21.42 Releases Critical Security Update
item.description: Red Enterprise Linux users of OpenShift Container Platform 4.21.42 receive a critical security update addressing bugs that could affect container runtime stability. The update is rated Critical by Red Hat Product Security, and CVSS scores via CVE links indicate high impact if unpatched. Administrators should apply the 4.21.42 update immediately and review CVSS scores to prioritize remediation.

item.description: Red Hat released a security update for python‑jwt on RHEL 7 ELS, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. Apply the python‑jwt update immediately to secure RHEL 7 ELS systems.

item.title: OpenShift 4.16.75 Releases Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released OpenShift Container Platform 4.16.75, fixing bugs and adding enhancements, including a security update. The update mitigates vulnerabilities that could enable unauthorized access or privilege escalation, with CVSS base scores in the CVE references, rated Important by Red Hat Product Security. Apply the 4.16.75 release promptly to obtain the latest patches and mitigations.

item.title: OpenShift 4.16.75 Releases Security Update for RHEL 9
item.description: Red Hat released OpenShift Container Platform 4.16.75 for RHEL 9, fixing multiple bugs and adding enhancements. The update includes a security fix for OpenShift 4.16, with a moderate CVSS base score, though no CVE IDs are listed. Security teams should apply the 4.16.75 update immediately to mitigate the identified vulnerabilities and maintain platform integrity.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Resteasy Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for Resteasy on RHEL 9.2 Update Services for SAP Solutions, fixing a critical REST flaw. The flaw, rated Important by Red Hat Product Security, lacks a public CVE ID but has a CVSS base score in the advisory. Apply the patch immediately; Red Hat recommends updating to Resteasy package or following vendor mitigation guidance.

item.title: Red Hat Releases osbuild-composer Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for osbuild-composer, addressing vulnerabilities affecting RHEL 8.4 Mission Critical Update Support and Extended Update Support Add-On. The update mitigates privilege escalation and memory corruption risks identified in the build orchestration engine, with CVSS scores available via referenced CVE links. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately; no workarounds are required to maintain build integrity.

item.title: OpenSSH SSHole Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-123158) Enables Remote Code Execution
item.description: OpenSSH servers are vulnerable to the SSHole authentication bypass (CVE-2026-123158), letting attackers submit oversized passwords for unauthenticated remote code execution. The flaw exploits improper length validation in password handling, enabling privilege escalation and root access on affected Linux systems. Administrators must apply the vendor‑issued patch or upgrade to the latest OpenSSH release immediately to mitigate the vulnerability.

item.title: Iris Ohyama Cloud Breach Exposes 7.7 Million Customer Records
item.description: Iris Ohyama suffered a cloud breach that exposed 7.7 million customer records, including identifiers, contact details, and purchase histories. The unauthorized access originated from a third‑party cloud service, with no evidence of financial fraud or credential theft reported. Iris Ohyama notified regulators, advised affected users to monitor accounts and change passwords, and is conducting a forensic investigation.

item.title: Brava Security Raises 15 Million Exiting Stealth Mode
item.description: Cybersecurity startup Brava Security has emerged from stealth mode following a 15 million dollar funding round. The vendor offers a multi-agent AI platform engineered to simulate attack activity by generating realistic threat telemetry. Security teams can utilize this generated telemetry mechanism to identify and resolve defensive coverage gaps across enterprise environments.

item.title: Refrigeration Attacks Exploit CVE‑2026‑96951 in Europe
item.description: European retailers’ refrigeration systems were hit by cyberattacks exploiting CVE‑2026‑96951, granting attackers unauthorized control over temperature settings. The flaw allows remote code execution through malformed configuration files, and a public PoC shows attackers can alter cooling cycles, risking spoilage. Patch Tuesday will deliver a fix; security teams should apply it promptly and monitor logs for anomalous temperature changes.

item.title: Storm-3358 Exploits SSRF and File Upload in ARTEX
item.description: Storm-3358 attackers exploited SSRF and file upload flaws in ARTEX. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted HTTP requests, enabling attackers to read internal resources and upload malicious payloads, potentially compromising system integrity. ARTEX has released a patch that validates input paths and restricts file types; security teams should apply the update immediately and enforce strict upload policies.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Keycloak 26.6.9 Security Update to Mitigate Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for Keycloak 26.6.9, fixing a flaw that could let attackers gain unauthorized access or elevate privileges within deployments. The vulnerability affects both standard and containerized installations, potentially impacting OpenShift and Kubernetes environments. Administrators should download the updated packages or pull the new images from the Red Customer Portal and redeploy Keycloak to maintain security.

item.title: CTM360 Exposes Fake Gift Card Scam Tactics
item.description: CTM360 uncovered a series of fake gift card scams that impersonate well-known brands and celebrities to trick consumers into providing personal data. The campaigns use deceptive verification steps and affiliate networks to harvest information and trigger unwanted subscriptions, exploiting social engineering rather than technical vulnerabilities. Security teams should educate users about verifying legitimate offers and monitor for unauthorized subscription charges.

item.title: Claude Code Option Exposes Credentials to Public GitHub
item.description: Claude Code’s ‘Yes, and don’t ask again’ option stores passwords and API keys in project settings, allowing them to be pushed to public GitHub repositories. Researchers uncovered 2,539 secrets in 1,994 public repos, affecting 63 organizations, proving a single approval can expose credentials. Teams should disable the option, audit settings, rotate exposed keys, and enable secret scanning to prevent leakage.

item.title: Claude Code Exposes Secrets via 'Don't Ask Again' Setting
item.description: Claude Code's 'Don't Ask Again' feature records passwords and API keys into project settings files, exposing them in 1,122 public GitHub repositories. The flaw saves the exact command, including secrets, into an unprotected file, letting anyone with repository access read credentials. Anthropic and vendors advise disabling the option, scanning for exposed secrets, and rotating credentials; no patch yet.

item.title: Storm-3358 Expands ARTEX Attacks on Finance
item.description: In October 2026, the financially motivated threat actor Storm‑3358 intensified attacks on financial institutions using the ARTEX agentic AI offensive framework. ARTEX leverages AI to automate credential harvesting and phishing, enabling attackers to bypass traditional security controls without requiring manual intervention. Security teams should monitor for ARTEX‑related indicators, enforce multi‑factor authentication, and update email filtering rules to mitigate emerging threats.

item.title: Insignary Releases Free Insignary-Chk Tool to Detect PHP2Shell and Node2Shell Exposure
item.description: Toronto, Canada, November 6th, 2026, CyberNewswire Free, read-only scanner helps organizations find Linux servers and container images exposed to two actively exploited vulnerabilities in PHP and Node.js Insignary, a global open-source security company, today released insignary-chk, a free tool that checks for PHP2Shell and Node2Shell, two recently disclosed runtime vulnerabilities affecting PHP and Node.js.

item.title: Anthropic Remote Root Vulnerability Detection and Patch
item.description: Anthropic’s remote root flaw lets attackers gain privileged access on inference servers via a buffer overflow in request parsing. The bug permits unauthenticated code execution with a CVSS score of 8.5, and a PoC has been shown in the wild. Anthropic issued a patch; users should update the inference engine and enforce strict input validation to mitigate the risk.

item.title: ChromeOS Update Fixes Multiple High‑Severity CVEs
item.description: Google ChromeOS Stable channel update addresses several memory corruption flaws affecting WebXR, WebGL, Media, CacheStorage, and Navigation. The CVEs, including CVE‑2026‑121076, CVE‑2026‑121208, CVE‑2026‑79235, and others, enable use‑after‑free or out‑of‑bounds reads that could lead to arbitrary code execution if exploited in the browser. All affected devices should install the new 16836.32.0 build or apply vendor‑supplied patches to mitigate the vulnerabilities.

item.title: Metasploit Unauth RCE in Perimeter Devices
item.description: Metasploit contains an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw affecting perimeter devices, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary code without credentials. The vulnerability is actively exploitable, with no known public exploit yet, but could allow full system compromise on affected devices. Security teams should deploy the latest Metasploit patch immediately and implement detection rules to monitor for exploitation attempts.

item.title: SharePoint CVE‑2025‑53770 Exploited by Storm‑2603
item.description: A remote code execution flaw, CVE‑2025‑53770, in Microsoft SharePoint was actively exploited by the Storm‑2603 threat actor. The vulnerability allows attackers to inject malicious scripts via crafted HTTP requests, enabling arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the SharePoint service account. Microsoft has released a patch; organizations should apply the update immediately and monitor for suspicious activity in SharePoint logs.

item.title: CISA Reports RCE Exploitation of CVE-2023-1380
item.description: CISA identified active exploitation of CVE-2023-1380, a remote code execution vulnerability in unspecified software. The flaw allows attackers to execute arbitrary code without authentication, potentially compromising system integrity and confidentiality. Immediate patching is required; apply vendor‑issued updates, enable network segmentation, enforce least‑privilege access controls, and monitor for suspicious activity to mitigate exposure.

item.title: Claude Dispatch Browser Extension Enables Code Execution
item.description: A code‑execution vulnerability in the Claude Dispatch browser extension allows attackers to run arbitrary code within the host environment. The flaw, identified as CVE‑2026‑119977, is exploitable via a malicious add‑on and could lead to credential theft or system compromise. Users should update to the latest extension version or disable the add‑on to eliminate the execution risk.

item.title: SonicWall SSLVPN MFA Bypass (CVE‑2026‑19868) Enables Remote Code Execution
item.description: SonicWall SSLVPN suffered a critical MFA bypass flaw (CVE‑2026‑19868) that lets attackers gain unauthenticated access to corporate networks. The vulnerability stems from improper validation of authentication tokens during the SSLVPN handshake, enabling remote code execution and credential‑reuse attacks. SonicWall urges immediate firmware updates and stricter MFA enforcement to mitigate the risk.

item.title: ESXi Ransomware Exploits Weak Access Controls
item.description: The ESXi hypervisor was hit by ransomware that exploited weak access controls and misconfigurations to gain administrative privileges. Attackers encrypted virtual machine files with a cryptolocker payload, demanding payment to restore access, and the breach was detected via anomalous credential usage. VMware issued a security advisory urging immediate patching, stricter ESXi authentication, and least‑privilege access controls to mitigate future attacks.
